script: "After six years, I told her I am tired—my proposal shattered everything.". I posted this around six months ago before I was really contemplating whether to still give the relationship a chance and whether to propose. I was already feeling like a ghost in my own house, chasing a girl who kept slipping away after the first kiss. She promised therapy, promised change, but every time I asked, she shrugged and said, "I'll do it later." I kept hoping she'd finally step up, because the future I imagined with her felt like a glow in the dark. Then came the pre‑wedding tradition—families gathering, couples shouting love in front of everyone. She stood there, all calm, and said, "I don't need a man to be complete, I am just a nice bonus." (Micro‑hook: "She said she doesn't need a man to be complete.") And she didn't even say "I love you" once. I felt invisible, like a ghost in a room full of people. The stakes? My heart, my time, my whole future. I'd already given up my own goals for her. If I didn't pull back, I'd lose who I am. I tried talking to her that night, said how hurt I was, how her words felt like a slap. She dismissed it, "You're overreacting, I am just independent." That's when I decided to stand up for myself. I took back the ring, said "enough," and walked away. I realized I'd been a total jerk, dragging us both through a mess for too long. Now I've found a sliver of respect for myself after neglecting my needs for way too long. I hope we both heal, but I am done being a ghost chasing a mirage.
